text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: 
[IMG]
 can be easily reduced using $\mathrm{Zn}-\mathrm{Hg}/\mathrm{HCl}$ to 
[IMG]


Reason $\mathrm{R}:\mathrm{Zn}-\mathrm{Hg}/\mathrm{HCl}$ is used to reduce carbonyl group to $-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-$ group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: $\text{Both}A\text{and}\mathrm{R}$ are true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
A is true but $\mathrm{R}$ is false
Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Clemmensen reduction ($\mathrm{Zn}-\mathrm{Hg}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$) reduces the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones to a $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-$ group, so R is true.

The substrate, 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one, carries a tertiary $-\mathrm{OH}$ group, which in hot concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ ionises to a tertiary carbocation and is replaced by $-\mathrm{Cl}$, so the reduction gives 2-chloro-2-methylpentane, not 2-methylpentan-2-ol.

The hydroxy compound shown in A is therefore not obtained, so A is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{Co}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond angle values in a fac- $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{3}\mathrm{Cl}_{3}]$ complex is/are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an octahedral complex any two ligands are either cis to each other (bond angle $90^{\circ }$) or trans ($180^{\circ }$).

In the fac isomer the three $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ ligands occupy the three corners of one triangular face of the octahedron, so each Cl is trans to an $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and every pair of Cl atoms is mutually cis.


[IMG]

All three Cl–Co–Cl angles are therefore $90^{\circ }$. A $180^{\circ }$ Cl–Co–Cl angle occurs only in the mer isomer, and $120^{\circ }$ does not occur in an octahedron.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ oxidises $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ in acidic and neutral/faintly alkaline solutions, respectively, to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$) is a strong oxidizing agent that can oxidize iodide ions ($\mathrm{I}^{-}$) to different products depending on the pH of the solution.

In acidic solutions, $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ oxidizes $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ to molecular iodine ($\mathrm{I}_{2}$) according to the following equation:

$2\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+16\mathrm{H}^{+}+10\mathrm{I}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+8\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}+5\mathrm{I}_{2}$

In neutral or faintly alkaline solutions, the oxidation product is different because the $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is oxidized to iodate ion ($\mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}$). The reaction in a neutral or slightly alkaline solution is as follows:

$2\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}+10\mathrm{I}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{MnO}_{2}+4\mathrm{OH}^{-}+5\mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}$

So according to the reactions above, in acidic solutions, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is oxidized to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ while in neutral or faintly alkaline solutions, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is oxidized to $\mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}$. Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option C: $\mathrm{I}_{2}&\mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Y the two Br atoms are meta to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (positions 3 and 5) and the nitrogen group is gone, so $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ must first become an $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ group that directs bromine and is then removed.

$\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ reduces $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ to $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, giving 4-methylaniline.

$-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ is the strongest ortho/para director, so $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$(aq) brominates both positions ortho to it, giving 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline; these positions are meta to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

$\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ at $0\text{–}5{}^{\circ }\text{C}$ converts $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ into $-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$, and $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{PO}{}_{2}$ replaces $-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ by H, giving 3,5-dibromotoluene (Y).

In (D), CuBr would replace $-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ by Br and give 3,4,5-tribromotoluene; (A) and (B) never remove the nitrogen group.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

solution.body:
Higher the value of $K_{a}$ or lower the value $pK_{a}$,  stronger will be the acid.


[IMG]


Presence of electron donating groups destabilises the  phenoxide ion, thus, reduces acidic nature of phenol.  Presence of electron withdrawing group stabilises the  phenoxide ion thus increase the acidic strength of phenol.  

Thus, order of acidic strength is:


[IMG]

$\therefore$ Order of $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ will be = b > d > a > c

Note :

Acid Strength : -

Acids : Acids are those molecules which donates $H^{+}$ ion in aqueous solution (water) and increases concentration of $H^{+}$ ion in water.

$H-A(aq)$ $⇌$ $H^{+}(aq)+A^{-}(aq)$

Dissociation constant of this reaction is $K_{a}$. It is called ionisation constant.

$\to$ So we can say if a acid form more $H^{+}$ ion after adding it in $H_{2}O$ then that acid is called strong acid. If acid produce less $H^{+}$ ion in $H_{2}O$ then that acid is weak acid.

$\to$ Acid Strength $\propto$ Stability of conjugate base.

$\to$ Acid Strength $\propto$ $K_{a}$

$\to$ Acid Strength $\propto \frac{1}{pK_{a}}$

Remember :

$pK_{a}=-\log K_{a}$

$=\log (K_{a})^{-1}=\log \frac{1}{K_{a}}$

$1\mathrm{L},0.02\mathrm{M}$ solution of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]$ Br is mixed with $1\mathrm{L},0.02\mathrm{M}$ solution of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$. The resulting solution is divided into two equal parts $(\mathrm{X})$ and treated with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution and $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ solution respectively as shown below:

$1\mathrm{L}$ Solution $(\mathrm{X})+\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution (excess) $⟶\mathrm{Y}$

$1\mathrm{L}$ Solution $(\mathrm{X})+\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ solution (excess) $⟶\mathrm{Z}$

The number of moles of $\mathrm{Y}$ and $\mathrm{Z}$ respectively are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mixing gives 2 L containing $0.02$ mol of each complex, so each 1 L part contains $0.01$ mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}$ and $0.01$ mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$.

Only ions outside the coordination sphere are free to precipitate: in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}$ the bromide is ionic, and in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ the sulphate is ionic, while the coordinated $\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ do not react.

With excess $\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}$, only the ionic bromide precipitates, so $0.01$ mol $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ gives $0.01$ mol $\mathrm{AgBr}$ (Y).

With excess $\mathrm{BaCl}{}_{2}$, only the ionic sulphate precipitates, so $0.01$ mol $\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ gives $0.01$ mol $\mathrm{BaSO}{}_{4}$ (Z).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

The wave function $(\Psi )$ of $2\mathrm{s}$ is given by

$\Psi _{2\mathrm{s}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2π}}\left (\frac{1}{a_{0}}\right )^{1/2}\left (2-\frac{r}{a_{0}}\right )e^{-r/2a_{0}}$

At $r=r_{0}$, radial node is formed. Thus, $r_{0}$ in terms of $a_{0}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A radial node is a distance $r_{0}$ (finite, non-zero) at which $\Psi _{2s}=0$.

In the given function, $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2π}}\left (\dfrac{1}{a_{0}}\right )^{1/2}$ is a non-zero constant and $e^{-r/2a_{0}}\neq 0$ for every finite $r$, so $\Psi _{2s}$ vanishes only when the bracket is zero:

$2-\dfrac{r_{0}}{a_{0}}=0\Rightarrow r_{0}=2a_{0}$

This is the single radial node of the 2s orbital ($n-l-1=2-0-1=1$).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Number of compounds from the following which will not dissolve in cold $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solutions but will dissolve in hot $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution is $________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cold $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ dissolves carboxylic acids, and cold $\mathrm{NaOH}$ dissolves carboxylic acids and phenols; esters dissolve only in hot $\mathrm{NaOH}$, which hydrolyses them to water-soluble carboxylate and alkoxide or phenoxide salts.

4-Methylbenzoic acid dissolves in cold $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$, and the two phenols, 2-hydroxyacetophenone and 3-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde, dissolve in cold $\mathrm{NaOH}$, so all three are excluded.

1-Isopropyl-3-methoxybenzene is an ether with no acidic hydrogen and is not cleaved even by hot $\mathrm{NaOH}$, so it is excluded.

The three esters, methyl benzoate, 4-methylphenyl methanoate and phenyl ethanoate, are insoluble in cold $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ and cold $\mathrm{NaOH}$ but dissolve in hot $\mathrm{NaOH}$ by saponification.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
An organic compound undergoes first-order decomposition. If the time taken for the $60%$ decomposition is $540\mathrm{s}$, then the time required for $90%$ decomposition will be $________ s. ($Nearest integer).

Given: $\ln 10=2.3;\log 2=0.3$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the first order reaction,

$k=\frac{1}{t}\ln \frac{a}{a-x}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t=\frac{1}{k}\ln \frac{a}{a-x}$

When reaction is $60%$ completed,

$x=\frac{60}{100}a=0.6a,t=540\text{seconds};$

$k=\frac{1}{t_{1}}\ln \frac{a}{a-0.6a}$

$\therefore$ $t_{1}=\frac{1}{k}\ln \frac{a}{0.4a}$

When reaction is $90%$ completed, i.e., $x=0.9a$

$\begin{array}{l} k=\dfrac{1}{t_{2}}\ln \dfrac{a}{a-0.9a} \\  \\ \Rightarrow t_{2}=\dfrac{1}{k}\ln \dfrac{a}{0.1a} \\  \\ \therefore \dfrac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{k}\ln \frac{a}{0.4a}}{\frac{1}{k}\ln \frac{a}{0.1a}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{540}{t_{2}}=\dfrac{\ln \frac{10}{4}}{\ln 10} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{540}{t_{2}}=\frac{2.3\log 10-2.3\log 4}{2.3\log 10}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{540}{t_{2}}=\frac{2.3-2.3(0.6)}{2.3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{540}{t_{2}}=0.4$

$\Rightarrow$ $t_{2}=\frac{540}{0.4}=1350$ sec
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following equation:

$2\mathrm{SO}_{2}(g)+\mathrm{O}_{2}(g)⇌2\mathrm{SO}_{3}(g),\Delta H=-190\mathrm{kJ}$

The number of factors which will increase the yield of $\mathrm{SO}_{3}$ at equilibrium from the following is $_______$.

A. Increasing temperature

B. Increasing pressure

C. Adding more $\mathrm{SO}_{2}$

D. Adding more $\mathrm{O}_{2}$

E. Addition of catalyst
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The reaction $2~\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})2\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}(\mathrm{g})$ is exothermic ($\Delta H=-190\text{kJ}$) and has $\Delta n_{g}=2-3=-1$.

A. Increasing temperature favours the endothermic (backward) reaction, so the yield of $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$ falls.

B. Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas (forward), so the yield rises.

C and D. Adding the reactant $\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$ or $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ makes $Q<K$, so the equilibrium shifts forward and the yield rises.

E. A catalyst ($\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ in the contact process) speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally: equilibrium is reached sooner, but the equilibrium yield is unchanged.

Thus B, C and D increase the yield of $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$, which is 3 factors.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift
